```ts
                params.deep && { color: 0x144ccd, x: 0, y: -40, blur: 30, spread: -15 },
                params.soft && { color: 0x6694ff, alpha: 0.5, x: 0, y: -20, blur: 15, spread: -4 },
                params.rim && { color: 0xffffff, alpha: 0.4, x: 0, y: -10, blur: 10, spread: -3, blend: 'add' },
                params.lip && { color: 0x2365ff, alpha: 0.15, x: 0, y: 3, blur: 3, spread: -1 },
            ];

            g.roundRect(180, 80, 200, 200, 40).fill({
                gradient: body,
                innerShadow: shadows.filter((s): s is InnerShadow => s !== false),
            });
        });

        return undefined;
    },
});
```

```ts
g.roundRect(0, 0, 200, 200, 40).fill({
    color: 0x0a0909,
    innerShadow: [
        { color: 0x144ccd, y: -40, blur: 30, spread: -15 },
        { color: 0xffffff, alpha: 0.4, y: -10, blur: 10, spread: -3, blend: 'add' },
    ],
});
```

An inner shadow moves a copy of the shape, shrinks it by `spread` and blurs it. What the copy no
longer covers is shaded. Shadows draw in order on top of the fill, gradients included, and a
`stroke()` after the fill lands on top of them. Inner shadows work on closed shapes.

| Option | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `color` | black | Shadow colour |
| `alpha` | 1 | Opacity, 0 to 1 |
| `x`, `y` | 0 | Offset in local units. Positive moves right and down. |
| `blur` | 0 | Gaussian standard deviation, in local units |
| `spread` | 0 | Grows the shadow inwards. Negative makes it thinner. |
| `blend` | `'normal'` | `'add'` brightens what is underneath |

The option names follow Figma's inner shadow, so a spec ports over option by option.

### Blur progressively

Live demo `effects-progressive` (source):

```ts
import { SilkGraphics, vertical } from 'pixi-silk';
import { defineDemo } from './runtime';

// Progressive blur: the violet hill is sharp at its bottom edge and melts at the top. The white
// bloom under it is painted plus-lighter, so where they overlap the violet lifts towards white.
export default defineDemo({
    title: 'Progressive blur',
    size: [560, 380],
    controls: {
        top: { type: 'range', label: 'blur at top', min: 0, max: 80, step: 1, value: 48 },
        bottom: { type: 'range', label: 'blur at bottom', min: 0, max: 20, step: 1, value: 1 },
        bloom: { type: 'toggle', label: 'plus-lighter bloom', value: true },
    },
    setup({ stage, params, tick }) {
        const g = new SilkGraphics();
        const violet = vertical([0x6a3cf0, 0x4b22c9]);
        let drawn = '';

        stage.addChild(g);
        tick((t) => {
            const sway = Math.sin(t * 0.6) * 0.04;
            const key = `${params.top}|${params.bottom}|${params.bloom}|${sway.toFixed(3)}`;

            if (key === drawn) return;
            drawn = key;
            g.clear();
            g.roundRect(80, 30, 400, 320, 18).fill(0x1c1c1e);
            g.save()
                .translateTransform(290, 245)
                .rotateTransform(-0.22 + sway)
                .ellipse(0, 0, 240, 112)
                .fill({ gradient: violet, blur: { from: params.top, to: params.bottom } })
                .restore();
            if (params.bloom) {
                g.ellipse(300, 318, 150, 30).fill({ color: 0xffffff, alpha: 0.5, blur: 18, blend: 'add' });
                g.ellipse(300, 318, 80, 12).fill({ color: 0xf6efff, alpha: 0.55, blur: 8, blend: 'add' });
            }
        });

        return undefined;
    },
});
```

```ts
g.area(points, 350, { smooth: 'monotone' }).fill({
    color: 0x5b2ee0,
    blur: { from: 20, to: 1, angle: Math.PI / 2 },
});
```

A `ProgressiveBlur` changes the blur across the shape. `from` is the blur at the start edge and
`to` at the far edge, along `angle` in radians. The default angle, `Math.PI / 2`, runs from top to
bottom.

### Limits

The blur is exact on straight edges and close on corners. Large blurs on complex paths, or on
the results of [shape operations](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/docs/shape-operations/), can round inner corners a little. For
those, a Pixi `BlurFilter` over the object still works. With `createSilkApp`, filters render at
the screen resolution.

Blurred paints are dithered like gradients, so a large soft shadow does not band. See
[Gradients](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/docs/gradients/#banding).

---

# Glass and glow

URL: https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/docs/glass-and-glow/
Area: Paint

> Frosted glass that blurs and bends what is behind it, and neon light that adds up to white, from the pixi-silk/glass and pixi-silk/glow entry points.

`pixi-silk/glass` draws panes of frosted glass over your scene. `pixi-silk/glow` stacks blurred
passes of one shape into neon light. Both are separate entry points, not part of the root import.

Live demo `glass-playground`: source at https://github.com/schmooky/pixi-silk/blob/main/apps/site/src/demos/glass-playground.demo.ts

```ts

const card = new Glass({ width: 300, height: 190, radius: 34, blur: 18, refraction: 16, dispersion: 0.4 });

card.content.addChild(new Text({ text: 'Frosted', style: { fill: 0xffffff } }));
card.set({ lightAngle: -Math.PI / 4, grain: 0.05 });
app.stage.addChild(card); // after the scene it frosts
```

The pane reads whatever is drawn behind it, blurs it and bends it along the curved rim. Labels and
icons go in `card.content`, which draws on top of the glass and stays sharp. `set()` changes
options later.

### Glass options

| Option | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `width`, `height` | 240, 160 | Pane size. The top-left corner is at (0, 0). |
| `radius` | 28 | Corner radius |
| `smoothing` | 0.6 | Squircle corners, 0 (circular) to 1 |
| `blur` | 18 | Backdrop blur radius |
| `refraction` | 14 | How far the rim bends the backdrop. Negative bends inwards. |
| `dispersion` | 0.35 | Colour split at the rim, 0 to 1 |
| `bevel` | 22 | Width of the curved rim |
| `frost` | 0.06 | Milky whitening, 0 to 1 |
| `saturation` | 1.2 | Colour boost of what shows through |
| `tint`, `tintAmount` | white, 0.04 | Coloured glass |
| `opacity` | 1 | Overall opacity |
| `lightAngle`, `light` | top left, 0.8 | Where the sheen comes from, in radians, and how bright it is |
| `grain` | 0.035 | Film grain |
| `shadow` | 0.3 | Soft shadow under the pane. 0 turns it off. |

### Where glass stops

The pane needs the canvas behind it. On WebGL, `Glass` turns on the renderer's back buffer the
first time it draws, so the first frame shows a plain pane. Pass `useBackBuffer: true` to
`createSilkApp` to have glass from the first frame. WebGPU reads the backdrop without a back
buffer. On any other renderer the pane draws a plain frosted fill.

Add the pane after the scene it frosts, since it only sees what is already drawn. It stays axis
aligned: scale it freely, but do not rotate it.

### Make neon with Glow

Live demo `glow-neon`: source at https://github.com/schmooky/pixi-silk/blob/main/apps/site/src/demos/glow-neon.demo.ts

```ts

const spark = new Glow({
    draw: (g) => bolt(g, -50, -70, 100, 140),
    layers: neon(0xffd60a, { size: 100 }),
});
```

`Glow` draws one shape several times, once per layer, each with its own fill, stroke, blend and
offset. `neon()` returns the five-layer recipe for a shape about `size` wide. Two blooms go behind
it. The core has a gradient, coloured drop glows and a pale inner shadow. A white copy added on top
burns the middle out, and a blurred white outline finishes it.

| `neon()` option | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `size` | 100 | Rough size of the shape. Every blur scales with it. |
| `intensity` | 1 | Strength of the bloom, 0 to about 2 |
| `core` | a radial gradient | Paint of the solid core |
| `surface` | `'dark'` | On `'light'` surfaces the passes paint normally, since added light would vanish on white |

`bolt()` and `drop()` add ready outlines. Any path works in `draw`, because a fill treats a path
as one shape.

### Light that adds up

Light does not cover what is under it, it adds to it. Set `blendMode = 'add'` on a graphics, or
`blend: 'add'` on one fill, and overlapping glows burn towards white. Figma calls this Plus
lighter. With a `blur` on the fill, a soft light is one ellipse.

Live demo `glow-button`: source at https://github.com/schmooky/pixi-silk/blob/main/apps/site/src/demos/glow-button.demo.ts

The border of this button is an open path. Its head leaves a gap with a star of light in it.

Live demo `glow-icons`: source at https://github.com/schmooky/pixi-silk/blob/main/apps/site/src/demos/glow-icons.demo.ts

Each icon is a large shape clipped by its tile. Its blur grows from the lit edge to the far side,
and an inner shadow pushed away from the light leaves a bright rim.

`Aurora` rises light in three colours from the bottom of a box and drifts slowly. `ray()`, `fan()`
and `spectrum()` build beams and prisms. The [Showcase](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/docs/showcase/) has the full scenes made
with them.

---

# Interaction and motion

URL: https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/docs/interaction-and-motion/
Area: Interface

> Pointer events test the painted shape, so rings are hollow and lines react only on their stroke. damp, Spring and ease move things the same at any refresh rate.

A SilkGraphics answers pointer events with the shape it paints, not its bounding box. The motion
helpers in the root import take the frame time, so an animation runs at the same speed on a 60 Hz
and a 144 Hz screen.

### React to the pointer

Demo sources run in the docs demo runner, `defineDemo({ setup({ stage, params, tick }) })`. In your own app, `stage` is `app.stage` (or a container on it), `params` holds the values of the demo controls, and `tick(fn)` is `app.ticker.add`, with `t` and `dt` in seconds.

Live demo `hit-test` (source):

```ts
import { SilkGraphics } from 'pixi-silk';
import { defineDemo } from './runtime';

// containsPoint() evaluates the real distance field: the ring is hollow, the line is only its stroke.
export default defineDemo({
    title: 'Hit testing',
    size: [480, 220],
    setup({ stage, tick }) {
        const items = [
            { draw: (g: SilkGraphics, c: number) => g.circle(100, 110, 60).stroke({ width: 18, color: c }) },
            { draw: (g: SilkGraphics, c: number) => g.roundRect(200, 50, 120, 120, 36, 0.6).fill(c) },
            {
                draw: (g: SilkGraphics, c: number) =>
                    g.polyline([350, 170, 390, 60, 450, 150]).stroke({ width: 10, cap: 'round', color: c }),
            },
        ].map((item) => {
            const g = new SilkGraphics();

            g.eventMode = 'static';
            g.cursor = 'pointer';
            stage.addChild(g);

            return { ...item, g, hover: false };
        });

        for (const item of items) {
            item.g.on('pointerover', () => (item.hover = true));
            item.g.on('pointerout', () => (item.hover = false));
        }
        tick(() => {
            for (const item of items) item.draw(item.g.clear(), item.hover ? 0x30d158 : 0x48484a);
        });
    },
});
```

Set `eventMode` and add listeners, as with any Pixi display object:

```ts
const button = new SilkGraphics();

button.eventMode = 'static';
button.cursor = 'pointer';
button.on('pointertap', () => console.log('tap'));
button.roundRect(0, 0, 160, 48, 24).fill(0x0a84ff);
```

The tap fires inside the rounded rect only, not in the corners its radius cuts away.

`containsPoint()` checks the object's bounds first. Then it runs the shader's distance functions
on the CPU for the primitives under the pointer, last drawn first. A point is inside when its
distance to the painted region is negative. So a stroked circle is a ring with no centre, a line
counts only within its stroke width, and a blurred paint counts only up to its geometric edge.

You can call it yourself:

```ts
if (g.containsPoint(g.toLocal(pointerGlobal))) {
    // hovered
}
```

In a large interactive scene, split independent targets into separate SilkGraphics objects. Each
one then tests only its own primitives. For drags, taps and long presses on any container, see
`trackGesture` in `pixi-silk/ui/gesture`.

### Move things at any refresh rate

Live demo `spring` (source):

```ts
import { Container } from 'pixi.js';
import { damp, SilkGraphics, Spring } from 'pixi-silk';
import { defineDemo } from './runtime';

// Frame-rate independent motion: the knob glides the same at 60, 120 or 144 Hz.
export default defineDemo({
    title: 'Spring',
    size: [480, 200],
    touchAction: 'none',
    controls: {
        stiffness: { type: 'range', label: 'stiffness', min: 40, max: 400, step: 1, value: 170 },
        damping: { type: 'range', label: 'damping', min: 4, max: 40, step: 1, value: 14 },
    },
    setup({ stage, params, tick }) {
        const g = new SilkGraphics();
        const hit = new Container();
        const x = new Spring(120);
        let glow = 0;
        let dragging = false;

        hit.eventMode = 'static';
        hit.hitArea = { contains: (px: number, py: number) => px >= 0 && px <= 480 && py >= 0 && py <= 200 };
        hit.on('pointerdown', (e) => {
            dragging = true;
            x.target = Math.min(440, Math.max(40, e.getLocalPosition(stage).x));
        });
        hit.on('globalpointermove', (e) => {
            if (dragging) x.target = Math.min(440, Math.max(40, e.getLocalPosition(stage).x));
        });
        hit.on('pointerup', () => (dragging = false));
        hit.on('pointerupoutside', () => (dragging = false));
        stage.addChild(g, hit);
        tick((_t, dt) => {
            x.stiffness = params.stiffness;
            x.damping = params.damping;
            x.step(dt);
            glow = damp(glow, dragging ? 1 : 0, 10, dt);
            g.clear();
            g.pill(40, 94, 400, 12).fill(0x2c2c2e);
            g.pill(40, 94, Math.max(12, x.value - 40), 12).fill(0x0a84ff);
            g.circle(x.value, 100, 22 + glow * 6).fill({ color: 0x0a84ff, alpha: 0.35 * glow, blur: 10 });
            g.circle(x.value, 100, 20).fill(0xffffff);
        });
    },
});
```

Easing by a fixed fraction per frame (`x += (target - x) * 0.1`) runs twice as fast on a 120 Hz
display. The helpers take the frame time in seconds instead:

```ts

x = damp(x, target, 10, dt);             // exponential approach, lambda is about 1 / seconds
angle = dampAngle(angle, target, 8, dt); // the shortest way around the circle

const spring = new Spring(0, 170, 26); // value, stiffness, damping
spring.target = 1;
app.ticker.add((t) => draw(spring.step(t.deltaMS / 1000)));

ease.outCubic(0.5); // also inOutCubic, inOutSine, outExpo
```

`damp` closes a fixed share of the gap per second, whatever the frame rate. `Spring.step()`
integrates in fixed sub-steps, so it stays stable when a frame takes long. `spring.settled` tells
you when to stop redrawing.

| Helper | Arguments | Use it for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `damp` | current, target, lambda, dt | A value that follows a target without overshoot |
| `dampAngle` | current, target, lambda, dt | An angle, the short way round |
| `Spring` | value (0), stiffness (170), damping (26) | Motion with overshoot and a settle |
| `ease` | t from 0 to 1 | Timed tweens |

### Roll a number with an odometer

Live demo `odometer` (source):

```ts
import { Container } from 'pixi.js';
import { SilkGraphics } from 'pixi-silk';
import { Odometer } from 'pixi-silk/ui/odometer';
import { defineDemo, INK, label } from './runtime';

// Tap the canvas to add some downloads. Bigger jumps count for longer, and a second tap while
// it counts skips to the end. The small readout below rolls frame numbers with a minimum width.
export default defineDemo({
    title: 'Odometer counter',
    size: [720, 240],
    touchAction: 'none',
    setup({ silk, stage, tick }) {
        const ticker = silk.app.ticker;
        const panel = new SilkGraphics();
        const downloads = new Odometer({ ticker, value: 12480, fontSize: 44 });
        const frame = new Odometer({
            ticker,
            minDigits: 4,
            thousands: '',
            fontSize: 18,
            color: INK.muted,
            duration: 0.06,
            speedUp: false,
        });
        const hit = new Container();
        let f = 0;

        panel.roundRect(140, 24, 440, 130, 22, 0.6).fill(INK.surface);
        downloads.position.set(360, 100);
        frame.position.set(360, 196);
        hit.eventMode = 'static';
        hit.hitArea = { contains: (x, y) => x >= 0 && y >= 0 && x <= 720 && y <= 240 };
        hit.cursor = 'pointer';
        hit.on('pointertap', () => {
            if (downloads.state.counting.value) {
                downloads.skip();

                return;
            }
            const big = Math.random() < 0.25;

            downloads.set(
                downloads.state.value.value + Math.round(big ? 2000 + Math.random() * 40000 : 1 + Math.random() * 90),
            );
        });
        stage.addChild(
            panel,
            label('Downloads', 360, 40, {}, 0.5),
            downloads,
            label('Frame', 360, 162, {}, 0.5),
            frame,
            hit,
        );
        tick((_t, dt) => {
            f += dt * 12;
            frame.set(Math.floor(f));
        });

        return undefined;
    },
});
```

```ts

const total = new Odometer({ value: 1250, decimals: 2, prefix: '$', fontSize: 44 });

total.set(9800); // counts up, longer for bigger jumps
total.skip(); // straight to the end
total.state.counting.subscribe((on) => console.log(on ? 'counting' : 'done'));
```

Every digit column rolls on its own. A column moves only while the one below it passes from 9 to
0, so carries ripple like a mechanical counter. Glyphs come from a bitmap font made from the text
style, so a frame only moves them, and one mask clips them all. `format(value)` returns the same
text without rolling, for labels and screen readers.

| Option | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | 0 | Start value |
| `decimals` | 0 | Digits after the point |
| `prefix`, `suffix` | none | Text around the number, such as a currency |
| `thousands`, `point` | `,` and `.` | Separators. `''` turns thousands off |
| `minDigits` | 1 | Smallest number of whole digits |
| `fontSize`, `color`, `textStyle` | 32, white | The look of the digits |
| `duration` | 0.9 | Count-up time in seconds for a small change |
| `speedUp` | true | Bigger jumps count for longer, up to three times |
| `easing` | `outCubic` | Easing of the count |
| `onDone` | none | Called with the value when the count ends |

### Redraw every frame

The simplest animation clears and redraws in the ticker. `clear()` keeps the GPU buffers, so a
redraw only uploads the new primitive data.

```ts
app.ticker.add((ticker) => {
    const t = ticker.lastTime / 1000;

    g.clear();
    g.arcSweep(80, 80, 44, -Math.PI / 2, Math.PI * 2 * (0.5 + 0.4 * Math.sin(t))).stroke({ width: 12, cap: 'round', color: 0x30d158 });
});
```

Put the parts that do not move in a second SilkGraphics and draw it once.
[Performance](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/docs/performance/) has the numbers for large scenes.

Slow shapes glide between pixels instead of snapping, because silk renders coordinates as given
and `createSilkApp` turns pixel rounding off. The [sub-pixel experiment](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/lab/04-subpixel/) shows it.

---

# Renderers

URL: https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/docs/renderers/
Area: Reference

> pixi-silk renders on WebGL2 by default and on WebGPU when you ask for it. How to pick one, set up your own Pixi app and turn on batching.

pixi-silk renders on WebGL2 by default and on WebGPU when you ask for it. Both run the same
shader, a GLSL program and its WGSL port, so a scene looks the same on either.

Live demo `webgpu`: source at https://github.com/schmooky/pixi-silk/blob/main/apps/site/src/demos/webgpu.demo.ts

### Pick a renderer

`createSilkApp` creates a WebGL2 app. Pass `preference: 'webgpu'` to use WebGPU where the browser
has it:

```ts

const silk = await createSilkApp({ parent: document.body, preference: 'webgpu' });

silk.app.renderer.name; // 'webgpu', or 'webgl' where the browser has no WebGPU
silk.app.stage.addChild(new SilkGraphics().circle(60, 60, 40).fill(0x30d158));
```

Pixi tries WebGPU first and falls back to WebGL2. When it gets WebGPU, `createSilkApp` loads the
WGSL shader before it resolves.

WebGL2 stays the default because every current browser has it and it starts faster. Choose WebGPU
when the rest of your app needs it.

### Use WebGPU in your own Pixi app

The WGSL shader lives in its own entry point, `pixi-silk/webgpu`, so WebGL2 apps never download
it. If you create the application yourself, call `enableWebGPU()` once, before the first
`SilkGraphics`:

```ts

const app = new Application();

await app.init({ preference: 'webgpu' });
enableWebGPU();
app.stage.addChild(new SilkGraphics().circle(60, 60, 40).fill(0x30d158));
```

Objects created before the call have no WebGPU program. Pixi skips them and logs "Mesh shader has
no gpuProgram". Calling `enableWebGPU()` in a WebGL2 app does nothing harmful.

### Batch objects into one draw

Batching is off by default. Call `enableSilkBatching()` before you create the objects:

```ts

enableSilkBatching();
const dot = new SilkGraphics().circle(0, 0, 4).fill(0x0a84ff);
```

It works on WebGL2 and on WebGPU. On WebGPU it also needs `enableWebGPU()`, which `createSilkApp`
calls for you. [Performance](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/docs/performance/#batch-many-objects) says what breaks a batch.

### Glass on both renderers

`Glass` from `pixi-silk/glass` reads the pixels behind it. On WebGL2 it reads the back buffer,
which it turns on the first time it draws. On WebGPU it copies the render target, so it needs no
back buffer.

### What differs

The two shaders are line-for-line ports. Three details differ because of the APIs:

| Detail | WebGL2 | WebGPU |
|---|---|---|
| Dither grain | rows counted from the bottom | rows counted from the top, so the grain is mirrored. Its strength is the same |
| Gradient ramp reads | the GPU's linear filter, which can round the blend weight to 8 bits | two exact texel loads, blended in the shader |
| Derivatives | `dFdx`, precision up to the GPU | `dpdx`, precision up to the GPU |

Edges can differ by a rounding step. Add `?renderer=webgpu` to a docs URL to run every demo on that
page on WebGPU.

---

# Resolution & DPR

URL: https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/docs/resolution/
Area: Reference

> createSilkApp maps the canvas 1:1 to device pixels, even at fractional DPRs, follows DPR changes and renders filters at screen resolution.

`createSilkApp` gives you a canvas whose pixels are the screen's pixels. Exact edges need that as
much as they need the shader: if the browser rescales the canvas, every edge goes soft.

Demo sources run in the docs demo runner, `defineDemo({ setup({ stage, params, tick }) })`. In your own app, `stage` is `app.stage` (or a container on it), `params` holds the values of the demo controls, and `tick(fn)` is `app.ticker.add`, with `t` and `dt` in seconds.

Live demo `resolution` (source):

```ts
import { SilkGraphics } from 'pixi-silk';
import { defineDemo } from './runtime';

// A Siemens star is the hardest test for anti-aliasing: every wedge narrows below a pixel.
export default defineDemo({
    title: 'Resolution',
    size: [480, 240],
    controls: {
        resolution: { type: 'select', label: 'resolution', options: ['device', '1x', '2x', '3x'], value: 'device' },
    },
    setup({ silk, stage, params, tick }) {
        const g = new SilkGraphics();
        let applied = '';

        stage.addChild(g);
        for (let i = 0; i < 36; i++) {
            const a = (i / 36) * Math.PI * 2;

            g.sector(240, 120, 110, a, a + Math.PI / 36).fill(0xffffff);
        }
        g.circle(240, 120, 110).stroke({ width: 1, color: 0x636366 });
        tick(() => {
            if (params.resolution === applied) return;
            applied = params.resolution;
            // createSilkApp sizes the backing store in device pixels; force 1x/2x/3x to compare
            silk.setResolution(applied === 'device' ? null : Number(applied[0]));
        });
    },
});
```

### Create a sharp canvas

```ts

const silk = await createSilkApp({
    parent: document.getElementById('stage')!,
    background: 0x000000,
    maxResolution: 3,
});

silk.app; // the Pixi Application
silk.width; // CSS pixels
silk.resolution; // device pixels per CSS pixel
silk.setResolution(1); // compare at 1x, null returns to devicePixelRatio
silk.destroy();
```

The canvas fills `parent`, so the parent needs a size. Every other option is a Pixi
`ApplicationOptions` field and passes through.

| Option | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `parent` | required | Element the canvas fills |
| `maxResolution` | `3` | Upper bound for the resolution, to cap memory and fill rate |
| `fixedResolution` | none | Forces a resolution instead of following `devicePixelRatio` |
| `onResize` | none | Called after every size or resolution change, with the size in CSS pixels |
| `inheritFilterResolution` | `true` | New Pixi filters render at the renderer resolution |
| `touchAction` | `'pan-y pinch-zoom'` | CSS `touch-action` of the canvas |
| `preference` | `'webgl'` | Renderer Pixi tries first. See [renderers](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/docs/renderers/) |

### What it sets up

The backing store is sized from `devicePixelContentBoxSize`, so one canvas pixel is one device
pixel, even at a DPR of 1.5 or 2.625. Rounding `cssWidth * dpr` yourself can be off by one pixel.
The browser then resamples the whole canvas and blurs it. Safari has no device pixel box, so there
the size is rounded.

The canvas follows DPR changes, such as browser zoom or a move to another display.

MSAA is off (`antialias: false`), because the shader already computes coverage. Pixel rounding is
off too (`roundPixels: false`), so slow motion moves by fractions of a pixel instead of snapping.

Pixi filters render at resolution 1 by default, which blurs everything behind a filter on a retina
screen. `createSilkApp` sets `Filter.defaultOptions.resolution` to `'inherit'`. Turn that off with
`inheritFilterResolution: false`.

Pixi sets `touch-action: none` on its canvas, which stops the page from scrolling on phones. The
default here lets the page scroll. Use `touchAction: 'none'` for a canvas that handles drags
itself.

### Your own Application

If you create the application yourself, use the same settings:

```ts
await app.init({
    preference: 'webgl',
    antialias: false,
    autoDensity: true,
    resolution: window.devicePixelRatio,
    roundPixels: false,
});
Filter.defaultOptions.resolution = 'inherit';
```

This does not size the backing store to exact device pixels or follow DPR changes. For that, use
`createSilkApp` or copy its `ResizeObserver` code.

### Render textures and filters

A `SilkGraphics` in a render texture or behind a filter is anti-aliased at that target's
resolution. Give render textures the renderer's resolution to keep them sharp on retina screens.
The [render texture experiment](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/lab/06-render-texture/) shows the difference.

---

# Performance

URL: https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/docs/performance/
Area: Reference

> What a SilkGraphics costs on the CPU and GPU, how batching joins objects into one draw, and how to keep static layers and large canvases cheap.

A `SilkGraphics` is one instanced draw call, whatever it contains. What you pay for is the CPU
work to rebuild it and the GPU work per covered pixel.

Demo sources run in the docs demo runner, `defineDemo({ setup({ stage, params, tick }) })`. In your own app, `stage` is `app.stage` (or a container on it), `params` holds the values of the demo controls, and `tick(fn)` is `app.ticker.add`, with `t` and `dt` in seconds.

Live demo `stress` (source):

```ts
import { Graphics } from 'pixi.js';
import { SilkGraphics } from 'pixi-silk';
import { defineDemo, INK, PALETTE, readout } from './runtime';

// Everything is rebuilt every frame: one SilkGraphics, one draw call, however many primitives.
export default defineDemo({
    title: 'Stress test',
    size: [720, 280],
    controls: {
        count: { type: 'range', label: 'primitives', min: 500, max: 30000, step: 500, value: 5000 },
    },
    setup({ stage, params, tick }) {
        const g = new SilkGraphics();
        // the stats sit in a strip above the drawing
        const strip = new Graphics().rect(0, 0, 720, 40).fill(INK.surface).rect(0, 40, 720, 1).fill(INK.line);
        const stats = readout('', 24, 13, { fontSize: 13 });

        stage.addChild(g, strip, stats);
        let cpu = 0;

        tick((t) => {
            const start = performance.now();

            g.clear();
            for (let i = 0; i < params.count; i++) {
                const a = i * 2.399963 + t * 0.2;
                const r = Math.sqrt(i / params.count) * 100;
                const x = 360 + Math.cos(a) * r * 2.6;
                const y = 160 + Math.sin(a) * r;

                if (i % 3 === 0) g.circle(x, y, 2.2).fill(PALETTE.pink);
                else if (i % 3 === 1) g.roundRect(x - 2, y - 2, 4, 4, 1).fill(PALETTE.blue);
                else g.line(x, y, x + 5, y + 2).stroke({ width: 1, color: PALETTE.green });
            }
            cpu = cpu * 0.9 + (performance.now() - start) * 0.1;
            stats.text = `${params.count} primitives   1 draw call   rebuilt in ${cpu.toFixed(1)} ms`;
        });
    },
});
```

### The cost model

| Cost | What it is |
|---|---|
| Draw calls | One per `SilkGraphics`. With batching on, a run of them shares one |
| CPU | 44 floats per primitive, written into a reusable buffer when you redraw. Rebuilding 50,000 primitives every frame takes about 12 ms on a laptop. A UI with hundreds of primitives costs well under 0.5 ms |
| GPU | Each primitive is one quad sized to its bounds plus a one-pixel margin, shaded once per covered pixel. A blur grows the quad by three sigma |
| Memory | Buffers grow to the largest frame and stay. Gradients share one 256x256 half-float atlas, one row per ramp |

GPU cost follows covered area, like any 2D renderer. A full-screen blurred shape costs more than a
thousand small dots.

### Batch many objects

Batching is off by default. `enableSilkBatching()` turns it on for objects created after the call.

Live demo `batching`: source at https://github.com/schmooky/pixi-silk/blob/main/apps/site/src/demos/batching.demo.ts

```ts

enableSilkBatching();
const dot = new SilkGraphics().circle(0, 0, 4).fill(0x0a84ff); // batched
const alone = new SilkGraphics({ batch: false }); // its own draw call
```

Consecutive `SilkGraphics` with the same blend mode and the same `dither`, `aaWidth` and
`minStrokePx` render in one draw. A filter, a mask, another kind of display object or a different
blend mode in between starts a new batch. Batching works on WebGL2 and on WebGPU.

A batch copies the instances and path data of its objects into one buffer. When none of them was
redrawn since the last frame, it copies only their matrices and tints.

### Keep frames cheap

Split static and dynamic parts. Draw backgrounds and fixed shapes once, and redraw only the parts
that change.

Move objects instead of redrawing them. Changing `position`, `rotation`, `scale` or `alpha` of a
`SilkGraphics` updates one matrix and costs nothing on the CPU side.

Create gradients once, at module scope. Identical ramps share an atlas row anyway, but reusing the
object skips parsing the stops again. The atlas has 256 rows. Past that, pixi-silk warns and reuses
row 0.

Put primitives that share a layer into one `SilkGraphics`, or turn on batching.

Cap the resolution of large canvases with `createSilkApp({ maxResolution: 2 })`. Fill rate grows
with the square of the resolution.

Stop redrawing when nothing moves. Check `Spring.settled`, or redraw only when the data changes.

---

# Glossary

URL: https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/docs/glossary/
Area: Reference

> Short definitions of anti-aliasing, MSAA, SSAA, FXAA, signed distance fields, coverage, device pixel ratio, squircles, OKLab, banding and dithering.

This page defines the terms used across these docs. Each entry starts with a one-sentence definition.

- **Aliasing** (jaggies, staircase artifacts): The jagged or crawling edges that appear when you sample a continuous shape at only one point per pixel. Each pixel is then either fully in or fully out.
- **Analytic anti-aliasing**: Anti-aliasing computed exactly per pixel from the shape's geometry, not from extra samples. pixi-silk derives coverage from the signed distance to the shape and the size of one device pixel.
- **Anti-aliasing** (antialiasing, AA): Techniques that remove the jagged "staircase" look of edges on a pixel grid. Each edge pixel gets a partial colour proportional to how much of it the shape covers.
- **Coverage**: The fraction of a pixel's area covered by a shape, from 0 to 1. Anti-aliasing uses coverage as the pixel's opacity along edges.
- **Device pixel**: One physical pixel of the display. A canvas is sharp only when each of its pixels maps to exactly one device pixel.
- **Device pixel ratio** (DPR, devicePixelRatio): The number of physical screen pixels per CSS pixel: 1 on standard displays, 2 or 3 on retina or HiDPI screens. Many laptops and phones have fractional ratios such as 1.25 or 1.5.
- **Dithering**: Adding a little structured noise (here ±½ of an 8-bit step) before quantising. It hides banding and leaves exact colours unchanged.
- **Draw call**: One command from the CPU telling the GPU to draw. Fewer draw calls usually mean better performance. Each SilkGraphics is one draw call.
- **FXAA** (fast approximate anti-aliasing): A cheap post-processing filter that detects and blurs high-contrast edges in the finished image. It softens detail and text and cannot recover geometry lost between pixels.
- **Gradient banding** (colour banding): Visible steps in a smooth gradient caused by 8-bit colour precision, most obvious in dark, wide gradients.
- **Hairline**: A line thinner than one device pixel. pixi-silk keeps hairlines one pixel wide and scales their opacity with their width, so they fade instead of breaking up.
- **Instanced rendering** (instancing): Drawing many copies of one mesh in a single draw call, each with its own data. pixi-silk draws every primitive of a SilkGraphics as one instance of a quad.
- **Monotone interpolation**: A curve through data points that never overshoots them. Peaks stay on the data and flat runs stay flat. pixi-silk uses Steffen's method (like d3's curveMonotoneX) for charts.
- **MSAA** (multisample anti-aliasing): A GPU technique that stores several coverage samples per pixel (typically 4) and averages them. In PixiJS, you enable it with antialias: true. By default it covers only the main canvas. Filters and render textures must opt in one by one.
- **OKLab**: A perceptual colour space by Björn Ottosson, where equal steps look equally different. Gradients interpolated in OKLab stay bright and even, without muddy midpoints.
- **Premultiplied alpha**: Storing colour already multiplied by opacity. Interpolating premultiplied colours prevents dark fringes when a gradient fades to transparent.
- **Signed distance field** (SDF): A function that returns the distance from any point to the nearest edge of a shape: negative inside, positive outside. Rendering a shape from its SDF gives exact edges at any scale.
- **Squircle** (superellipse corner, continuous corner): A rounded rectangle whose corners are superellipse arcs, so curvature grows gradually from the straight edge instead of jumping. iOS app icons and cards use it.
- **SSAA** (supersampling): Anti-aliasing by rendering at a higher resolution and downscaling. It is simple and high quality. Memory and fill-rate costs grow with the scale factor squared.
- **Tessellation**: Converting curves and shapes into triangles for the GPU. PixiJS Graphics tessellates when you draw, so curves become polygons with a fixed number of segments.

---

# How it works

URL: https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/docs/how-it-works/
Area: Architecture

> One instanced quad per primitive, an exact signed distance per pixel, coverage from screen-space derivatives and dithered OKLab gradient ramps.

This page walks through the shader, from the instance buffer to the colour of one pixel. You do not
need it to use pixi-silk. Read it when you want to know why an edge, a join or a gradient looks the
way it does. [Anti-aliasing compared](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/docs/anti-aliasing-compared/) sets the approach next to MSAA
and the other options.

### One instance per primitive

`SilkGraphics` is a Pixi `Mesh` that draws an instanced unit quad. Each primitive you add is one
instance of 44 floats, eleven `vec4` attributes:

| Attribute | Holds |
|---|---|
| `aBounds` | local bounds, including the stroke outset and three sigma of blur |
| `aShape0` to `aShape2` | the shape's parameters |
| `aMeta` | primitive type, flags, stroke width, blur sigma |
| `aFill`, `aStroke` | premultiplied colours |
| `aGrad`, `aPaint` | gradient geometry, kind, atlas row and extend mode |
| `aDash` | dash, gap, offset and stroke alignment |
| `aFx` | spread, progressive blur, and the object index when batched |

The vertex shader expands the quad to the bounds plus an anti-aliasing margin. The margin is in
device pixels. It uses the smallest singular value of the local-to-pixel Jacobian, so it stays right
at any zoom and for rotated or skewed objects.

### Exact distance, analytic coverage

For every pixel, the fragment shader computes the signed distance `d` from the pixel centre to the
shape, negative inside. Each primitive kind has its own exact function: rounded boxes with
per-corner radii and superellipse corners, ellipses, arcs, sectors, capsules, hearts, stars,
triangles and free paths. The shader turns the distance into coverage with a box filter one device
pixel wide:

```glsl
float px = sqrt(abs(dFdx(p).x * dFdy(p).y - dFdx(p).y * dFdy(p).x)); // one device pixel, in local units
float coverage = clamp(0.5 - d / px, 0.0, 1.0);
```

The one detail that matters is `px`. It comes from screen-space derivatives, so the filter is one
device pixel wide at 1000x zoom, when rotated, and inside filters and render textures. With `blur`,
the box filter becomes a gaussian, `0.5 - 0.5 * erf(d / (sigma * sqrt(2)))`. `spread` moves the
distance before the blur, which grows or shrinks the shape.

### Fill and stroke in one pass

A primitive with both a fill and a stroke is shaded once. The shader computes the coverage of the
whole shape and of the stroke band, and splits each pixel into stroke and fill outside the stroke.
No anti-aliased fill edge shows through an inner stroke.

### Paths

A stroked path is one distance field. Its segments sit in a float texture, and the shader takes the
nearest of their segments, caps and joins, the way Canvas 2D defines a stroke. Joins are miter (the
default, cut to a bevel past `miterLimit`), bevel or round. Every pixel is shaded once, so a
translucent path never blends twice where it overlaps itself.

Long subpaths are split into chunks of 32 segments. Each chunk also checks the segments of other
chunks that come near it, found on the CPU. A pixel goes to the chunk with the nearest segment, so
it is shaded once even where the path crosses itself.

A filled path stores its edges the same way. The distance is the nearest edge, and the sign comes
from even-odd crossings. Tapered strokes keep one instance per segment, with the exact distance to
a capsule whose ends have different radii.

### Unions and shape operations

`union: true` on a fill or stroke stores every shape of the path as a record in the path texture.
The shader takes the nearest distance, so overlapping shapes paint as one.

[Shape operations](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/docs/shape-operations/) use the same records, each with an op. The shader folds
them on a small stack. The minimum of two distances is a union and the maximum an intersection.
`max(a, -b)` subtracts b from a, and `max(min(a, b), -max(a, b))` excludes. All four are exact on
the outline.

### Areas

Chart areas are split into vertical columns that tile exactly. Shared column edges get no
anti-aliasing margin. Only the top and bottom edges do, so a translucent fill has no seams.

### Hairlines

A stroke thinner than `minStrokePx` (one device pixel by default) is drawn at that width, with its
alpha scaled down by the ratio. The amount of ink stays the same, and thin lines never break into
dots.

### Gradients

Stops are interpolated premultiplied, in OKLab by default, and baked into a shared 256x256 RGBA16F
atlas, one reference-counted row per ramp. The shader adds plus or minus half an 8-bit step of
interleaved gradient noise to gradients and blurs. That removes banding and leaves exact 8-bit
colours alone. `dither: 0` turns it off.

### Batching

With `enableSilkBatching()`, consecutive objects copy their instances into one buffer. Each
instance carries its object index in `aFx.w`. The vertex shader reads that object's matrix, tint and
path texel base from a small table texture. [Performance](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/docs/performance/) covers when a batch
breaks.

### Hit testing

The same distance functions run on the CPU. `containsPoint` tests the real shape, holes and stroke
widths included. [Interaction and motion](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/docs/interaction-and-motion/) shows it in use.

### WebGPU

The WGSL shader is a line-for-line port of the GLSL one. [Renderers](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/docs/renderers/) lists the
small differences.

---

# Anti-aliasing compared

URL: https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/docs/anti-aliasing-compared/
Area: Architecture

> MSAA, resolution, curve smoothness, supersampling, FXAA, @pixi/graphics-smooth and analytic SDF anti-aliasing in PixiJS v8, compared, with fixes by symptom.

Anti-aliasing gives each edge pixel a partial colour, in proportion to how much of it the shape
covers. PixiJS v8 offers five ways to get there. pixi-silk adds a sixth: it computes coverage from
each shape's exact signed distance, per pixel. That is what the rest of the docs mean when they say
an edge stays sharp at any zoom, rotation and device pixel ratio.

### The options at a glance

| Technique | How to turn it on in PixiJS v8 | Edge quality | Cost | Applies to |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| MSAA | `app.init({ antialias: true })` | 4 samples, so 5 coverage levels per edge pixel | memory bandwidth, a resolve pass | the main canvas. Render textures and filters opt in |
| Higher resolution | `resolution: devicePixelRatio, autoDensity: true` | smaller stairs, still aliased | fill rate grows with DPR squared | everything |
| Curve smoothness | `app.init({ bezierSmoothness: 0.9 })` | fewer facets on curves, edges still aliased | more triangles | Graphics curves |
| Supersampling | draw into a 2x render texture, then draw it scaled down | high | 4x the pixels and an extra texture | what you draw into it |
| FXAA | a post-process filter | softer edges, blurred detail and text | one full-screen pass | the filtered object |
| Analytic SDF (pixi-silk) | `new SilkGraphics()` | exact coverage, continuous | one instanced draw call per object | everywhere, filters and render textures included |

### MSAA in PixiJS v8

```ts

const app = new Application();

await app.init({
    antialias: true, // MSAA on the main canvas
    resolution: window.devicePixelRatio,
    autoDensity: true,
});
```

MSAA belongs to a render target, so it does not follow your objects. Render textures are not
multisampled unless you create them with `antialias: true`. Filters render into their own targets
without MSAA and at resolution 1, unless you change both.

MSAA works for large shapes at rest. UI and charts show where it stops:

- Slowly moving or rotating edges jump between the five coverage levels, which reads as shimmer.
- Lines thinner than a pixel fall between the four samples and look dotted.
- Zooming in shows the facets of curves, because Graphics fixed its triangles when you drew them.

### Analytic anti-aliasing

A signed distance field gives the distance from any point to the shape's edge. pixi-silk evaluates
each primitive's exact distance per pixel and turns it into coverage over one device pixel:

```glsl
float px = sqrt(abs(dFdx(p).x * dFdy(p).y - dFdx(p).y * dFdy(p).x)); // one device pixel, in shape units
float coverage = clamp(0.5 - d / px, 0.0, 1.0); // d: signed distance to the edge
```

The pixel size comes from screen-space derivatives. So the result holds at any scale, rotation,
resolution and render target, with nothing to tessellate and no samples to miss. Each
`SilkGraphics` draws all its primitives in one instanced call. [How it works](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/docs/how-it-works/)
follows the shader step by step.

```ts

const { app } = await createSilkApp({ parent: document.body });
const g = new SilkGraphics();

g.circle(200, 150, 80).stroke({ width: 2, color: 0x64d2ff });
g.roundRect(100, 60, 200, 180, 40, 0.6).stroke({ width: 0.5, color: 0xffffff });
app.stage.addChild(g);
```

The circle is exact at any zoom. The half-pixel stroke is drawn one pixel wide at half the alpha,
so it never breaks up. `createSilkApp` keeps MSAA off, because it would only cost bandwidth.

Analytic anti-aliasing has limits too. It applies to what `SilkGraphics` draws, not to sprites or
Pixi `Graphics`. GPU cost follows covered area, so a large blurred shape costs more than many small
ones.

### Fix a symptom

Most of these fixes work with plain `Graphics`. The last column is the pixi-silk route.

| You see | Cause | Fix in PixiJS | With pixi-silk |
|---|---|---|---|
| Jagged, stair-stepped edges | `antialias` is `false` by default | `app.init({ antialias: true })` | `SilkGraphics` computes coverage itself |
| Circles look like polygons when zoomed | Graphics cuts curves into segments when you draw | raise `bezierSmoothness`, or redraw at the final scale | curves are evaluated per pixel |
| Thin lines flicker, look dotted or vanish | a sub-pixel line covers a fraction of each pixel, and samples miss it | keep strokes at least one device pixel wide | hairlines fade instead of thinning. See [strokes and dashes](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/docs/strokes-and-dashes/) |
| Everything is a little blurry on retina screens | the canvas has fewer pixels than the screen, or was rounded at a fractional DPR | `resolution: devicePixelRatio, autoDensity: true` | `createSilkApp` maps canvas pixels 1:1. See [resolution](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/docs/resolution/) |
| Content behind a filter is blurry | filters render at resolution 1 | `Filter.defaultOptions.resolution = 'inherit'` | `createSilkApp` sets it for you |
| Gradients show bands | 8-bit colour, with no dither in `FillGradient` | none built in | half-float ramps, OKLab and dither. See [gradients](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/docs/gradients/) |
| Slow motion snaps from pixel to pixel | `roundPixels: true` | keep `roundPixels: false` | the default in `createSilkApp` |

### @pixi/graphics-smooth on PixiJS v8

[`@pixi/graphics-smooth`](https://github.com/pixijs-userland/graphics-smooth) is the community
plugin that made v7 `Graphics` smooth. Its `SmoothGraphics` class anti-aliases in the shader,
without MSAA. Its 1.1 line requires PixiJS 7.2 or a newer v7, and as of September 2026 there is no
v8 release on npm. On v8, `SilkGraphics` fills that role with a v8-style API.

```ts nocheck
// PixiJS v7 + @pixi/graphics-smooth
const g = new SmoothGraphics();
g.lineStyle({ width: 2, color: 0xffffff });
g.beginFill(0x1c1c1e);
g.drawRoundedRect(0, 0, 200, 80, 16);
g.endFill();
g.drawCircle(40, 40, 12);
```

```ts
// PixiJS v8 + pixi-silk
const g = new SilkGraphics();
g.roundRect(0, 0, 200, 80, 16).fill(0x1c1c1e).stroke({ width: 2, color: 0xffffff });
g.circle(40, 40, 12).stroke({ width: 2, color: 0xffffff });
```

| v7 call | SilkGraphics |
|---|---|
| `beginFill(c, a)` to `endFill()` | `shape().fill({ color: c, alpha: a })` |
| `lineStyle({ width, color, alpha })` | `shape().stroke({ width, color, alpha })` |
| `drawRect`, `drawRoundedRect`, `drawCircle`, `drawEllipse` | `rect`, `roundRect`, `circle`, `ellipse` |
| `moveTo`, `lineTo`, `bezierCurveTo` | the same, then `fill()` or `stroke()` |
| `arc(...)` | `arc(...)`, which starts its own subpath, or `arcSweep(...)` |
| `LINE_SCALE_MODE.NONE` | not built in. Divide the width by the scale |

PixiJS v8 changed the Graphics API itself. The [PixiJS v8 migration guide](https://pixijs.com/8.x/guides/migrations/v8)
covers the upgrade, and [migrating from Graphics](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/docs/migrating-from-graphics/) covers how v8
`Graphics` and `SilkGraphics` differ.

### Which one to use

For sprites and textures only, skip MSAA. The GPU filters textures already.

For a few large shapes and no zoom, `antialias: true` with `resolution: devicePixelRatio` is
enough.

For UI, charts, icons, thin lines and vector content that zooms or rotates, use `SilkGraphics` and
keep `antialias: false`. The same holds for content behind filters or in render textures.

The [infinite zoom](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/lab/03-zoom/) and [sub-pixel motion](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/lab/04-subpixel/) experiments at the end
of this page show the difference full screen.

### References

- PixiJS v8 [Graphics API](https://pixijs.download/release/docs/scene.Graphics.html) and the
  [issue on smoother curves in v8](https://github.com/pixijs/pixijs/issues/9831).
- Inigo Quilez, [2D distance functions](https://iquilezles.org/articles/distfunctions2d/).
- web.dev, [pixel-perfect rendering with devicePixelContentBox](https://web.dev/articles/device-pixel-content-box).
- Glossary: [MSAA](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/docs/glossary/#msaa), [SSAA](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/docs/glossary/#ssaa), [FXAA](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/docs/glossary/#fxaa)
  and [signed distance field](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/docs/glossary/#signed-distance-field).

---

# Layout engine

URL: https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/docs/layout-engine/
Area: Architecture

> pixi-silk/layout is the flex engine under SmartContainer and FlexContainer: plain nodes, CSS flexbox styles, measure functions and incremental passes.

`pixi-silk/layout` lays out a tree of plain nodes with CSS flexbox. It has no Pixi in it, so it
runs in tests, workers and on a server. [Layout](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/docs/layout/) wraps it in Pixi containers.
Read this page when you want the engine without Pixi, or need to know why a box ended up where it did.

### Lay out a tree

```ts

const root = new LayoutNode({ direction: 'row', gap: 8, padding: 16 });
const icon = new LayoutNode({ width: 100 });
const label = new LayoutNode({ grow: 1 });

root.add(icon).add(label);
root.calculate(400, 120);

label.layout; // { x: 124, y: 16, width: 260, height: 88 }
```

The label starts after the padding, the icon and the gap (16 + 100 + 8), takes the rest of the
width and stretches to the content height. `calculate(width, height)` lays out the whole tree, and
each node's `layout` holds its box relative to its parent. Leave a size out to fit that axis to
the content.

A node has a style, children and an optional `measure` function. `setStyle()` replaces the style
and `updateStyle()` merges into it. `add()`, `remove()` and `clear()` change the children.

### Styles

The style follows CSS flexbox, with `box-sizing: border-box` everywhere and shorter names.
Alignment values are `start`, `center`, `end`, `stretch` and, for items, `baseline`.

| Group | Fields |
| --- | --- |
| Container | `direction` (`row`, `column` and their `-reverse`), `wrap`, `gap`, `rowGap`, `columnGap`, `padding`, `justifyContent`, `alignItems`, `alignContent` |
| Item | `grow` (0), `shrink` (1), `basis` (`auto`), `alignSelf`, `margin` |
| Size | `width`, `height`, `minWidth`, `minHeight`, `maxWidth`, `maxHeight`, `aspectRatio` |
| Position | `position: 'absolute'` with `top`, `right`, `bottom`, `left` or `inset`, and `display: 'none'` |

Sizes are pixels, a percent of the parent's content box such as `'50%'`, or `'auto'`. Padding and
margin take one value, or two, three or four as in CSS. An `auto` margin takes the free space,
which centres an item or pushes it to the far end. Anchors of absolute items may be percents.

### How a pass computes

Each container first works out the basis of its items: the `basis`, else the `width` or `height`,
else the measured content. It breaks items into lines when `wrap` is on, then shares out the free
space of each line.

Grow and shrink run the CSS loop. Items that hit their `min` or `max` freeze there, and the rest
of the space goes round again until nothing changes. Shrinking is weighted by the basis, as in a
browser, so a wide item gives up more than a narrow one.

Then the cross axis. Lines are placed by `alignContent`, and items in a line by `alignItems` or
their `alignSelf`. A stretched item gets the line's cross size and lays out its own children
again at that size.

### Measure content

A leaf with content, such as text or a sprite, gets a `measure` function. It receives the space
offered and returns the content size, without padding. Either argument is `Infinity` when that
axis is free.

```ts

const charWidth = 9;
const lineHeight = 20;
const copy = 'Tap a card to open it in full view';

const text = new LayoutNode({}, (availableWidth) => {
    const perLine = Math.max(1, Math.floor(availableWidth / charWidth));
    const lines = Math.ceil(copy.length / perLine);

    return { width: Math.min(copy.length, perLine) * charWidth, height: lines * lineHeight };
});

new LayoutNode({ direction: 'column', width: 160 }).add(text).calculate();
```

In a 160-wide column the copy wraps at 17 characters a line, so the function returns 153 by 40.
The column then stretches the node to its full width of 160. Return a
`baseline` too, the distance from the top to the first baseline, and `alignItems: 'baseline'`
lines up text in a row.

### Incremental passes

Changing a style, adding or removing a child, or calling `markDirty()` marks the node and its
ancestors dirty. The next `calculate()` skips every clean subtree whose space did not change. A
measured leaf caches its size per available space, so it is measured again only after
`markDirty()`. Call it when the text or texture behind a leaf changes.

### Differences from CSS

The engine follows CSS where results differ in practice. A few things are simpler.

| Topic | What the engine does |
| --- | --- |
| Minimum size | An item's default minimum is 0, not its content size. Set `minWidth` or `shrink: 0` to keep it from shrinking below its content |
| Aspect ratio | A stretched cross size wins over `aspectRatio`, as in CSS. Set `alignSelf` to keep the ratio |
| Baseline | A container's baseline is its first item's. Only measured leaves report one of their own |
| Absolute items | Without anchors they sit where `justifyContent` and `alignItems` put them, not at their static position |
| Not there | `order`, `overflow`, borders and `flex-basis: content` |

The engine knows nothing about transforms. FlexContainer measures rotated children unrotated and
gives them their box as if they were not rotated.

---

# API reference

## ConicGradient (Class, `pixi-silk`)

URL: https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/classes/ConicGradient/

```ts
import { ConicGradient } from 'pixi-silk';
```

An angular ramp around a centre. On arcs it follows the arc. Create it with [conic](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/functions/conic/).

| ------ | ------ |

## Gradient (Class, `pixi-silk`)

URL: https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/classes/Gradient/

```ts
import { Gradient } from 'pixi-silk';
```

Base class of all gradients. Stops are interpolated premultiplied (OKLab by default), baked into a
shared half-float atlas and dithered when sampled, which hides banding.

A gradient is read when a shape is filled or stroked. Changing its points later does not change
shapes already painted: paint them again. The atlas holds 256 ramps in use at once, and
gradients with the same stops, space and easing share one.

### Extended by

- [`ConicGradient`](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/classes/ConicGradient/)
- [`LinearGradient`](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/classes/LinearGradient/)
- [`MeshGradient`](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/classes/MeshGradient/)
- [`PathGradient`](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/classes/PathGradient/)
- [`RadialGradient`](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/classes/RadialGradient/)

### Constructors

#### Constructor

```ts
new Gradient(options: GradientOptions): Gradient;
```

##### Parameters

| Parameter | Type |
| ------ | ------ |
| `options` | [`GradientOptions`](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/interfaces/GradientOptions/) |

##### Returns

`Gradient`

### Properties

| Property | Modifier | Type | Description | Defined in |
| ------ | ------ | ------ | ------ | ------ |
|  `easing` | `readonly` | [`Easing`](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/types/Easing/) | How the ramp moves between stops. | [gradient.ts:149](https://github.com/schmooky/pixi-silk/blob/main/packages/pixi-silk/src/gradient.ts#L149) |
|  `extend` | `readonly` | [`ExtendMode`](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/types/ExtendMode/) | What the gradient does outside 0..1. | [gradient.ts:151](https://github.com/schmooky/pixi-silk/blob/main/packages/pixi-silk/src/gradient.ts#L151) |
|  `space` | `readonly` | [`ColorSpace`](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/types/ColorSpace/) | Interpolation space. | [gradient.ts:147](https://github.com/schmooky/pixi-silk/blob/main/packages/pixi-silk/src/gradient.ts#L147) |
|  `units` | `readonly` | [`GradientUnits`](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/types/GradientUnits/) | Coordinates of the gradient's points and radii. | [gradient.ts:153](https://github.com/schmooky/pixi-silk/blob/main/packages/pixi-silk/src/gradient.ts#L153) |

## MeshGradient (Class, `pixi-silk`)

URL: https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/classes/MeshGradient/

```ts
import { MeshGradient } from 'pixi-silk';
```

A smooth colour surface through a grid of control colours, like a gradient mesh in Illustrator.
Colours blend with a bicubic spline in its `space` (OKLab by default), so falloffs stay soft in
both directions. The surface is baked at 16x16 samples.
Create it with [mesh](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/functions/mesh/).

## Spring (Class, `pixi-silk`)

URL: https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/classes/Spring/

```ts
import { Spring } from 'pixi-silk';
```

Damped harmonic spring with unit mass, integrated in fixed 1/240 s sub-steps. `stiffness` and
`damping` follow the usual UI spring convention. The defaults are 170 and 26.

### Constructors

#### Constructor

```ts
new Spring(
   value?: number, 
   stiffness?: number, 
   damping?: number
): Spring;
```

Starts at rest at `value`, with its target there too.

| Parameter | Type | Default value |
| ------ | ------ | ------ |
| `value` | `number` | `0` |
| `stiffness` | `number` | `170` |
| `damping` | `number` | `26` |

##### Returns

`Spring`

### Properties

| Property | Type | Default value | Description | Defined in |
| ------ | ------ | ------ | ------ | ------ |
|  `damping` | `number` | `undefined` | Friction. Lower bounces more. Default 26. | [motion.ts:38](https://github.com/schmooky/pixi-silk/blob/main/packages/pixi-silk/src/motion.ts#L38) |
|  `stiffness` | `number` | `undefined` | Pull towards the target. Higher is faster. Default 170. | [motion.ts:36](https://github.com/schmooky/pixi-silk/blob/main/packages/pixi-silk/src/motion.ts#L36) |
|  `target` | `number` | `undefined` | Value the spring moves towards. | [motion.ts:32](https://github.com/schmooky/pixi-silk/blob/main/packages/pixi-silk/src/motion.ts#L32) |

### Accessors

#### settled

##### Get Signature

```ts
get settled(): boolean;
```

True once the spring is within 1e-4 of its target and its speed is below 1e-4.

##### Returns

`boolean`

### Methods

```ts

```

Advances the spring by `dtSeconds`, capped at 0.1 s so a stalled tab does not jump, and returns the new value.

## catmullRom (Function, `pixi-silk`)

URL: https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/functions/catmullRom/

```ts
import { catmullRom } from 'pixi-silk';
```

```ts
function catmullRom(
   flat: number[], 
   closed?: boolean, 
   step?: number, 
   alpha?: number
): number[];
```

Samples a centripetal Catmull-Rom spline through flat points. It has no cusps or self-loops
within a segment. `closed` adds the segment back to the first point. `step` is the target sample
spacing in local units, at most 64 per segment. `alpha` 0.5 is centripetal (0 uniform, 1
chordal). Fewer than 3 points come back as a copy.

### Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default value |
| ------ | ------ | ------ |
| `flat` | `number`[] | `undefined` |
| `closed` | `boolean` | `false` |
| `step` | `number` | `2` |
| `alpha` | `number` | `0.5` |

### Returns

`number`[]

## conic (Function, `pixi-silk`)

URL: https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/functions/conic/

```ts
import { conic } from 'pixi-silk';
```

```ts
function conic(stops: StopInput[], options?: Omit<ConicGradientOptions, "stops">): ConicGradient;
```

Conic (angular) gradient. On arcs and sectors it spans the arc by default, so a ring's ramp
always runs from its start cap to its end cap.

| `options` | `Omit`\<[`ConicGradientOptions`](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/interfaces/ConicGradientOptions/), `"stops"`\> |

[`ConicGradient`](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/classes/ConicGradient/)

## damp (Function, `pixi-silk`)

URL: https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/functions/damp/

```ts
import { damp } from 'pixi-silk';
```

```ts
function damp(
   current: number, 
   target: number, 
   lambda: number, 
   dtSeconds: number
): number;
```

Exponential approach: returns `current` moved towards `target` over `dtSeconds`. `lambda` is
about 1 / seconds, higher is snappier. It never reaches the target exactly.

### Parameters

| Parameter | Type |
| ------ | ------ |
| `current` | `number` |
| `target` | `number` |
| `lambda` | `number` |
| `dtSeconds` | `number` |

### Returns

`number`

## enableSilkBatching (Function, `pixi-silk`)

URL: https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/functions/enableSilkBatching/

```ts
import { enableSilkBatching } from 'pixi-silk';
```

```ts
function enableSilkBatching(): void;
```

Turns on batching across objects, which is off by default. Runs of consecutive SilkGraphics with
the same blend mode and settings then render in one draw call. Only objects created after the
call take part, and an object with `batch: false` never does. There is no call to turn it off. Each renderer gets
the pipe the first time it draws one of them, so you can call it before or after creating the
Application. It is safe to call again.

It works with WebGL2 and with WebGPU. On WebGPU, call `enableWebGPU()` too ([createSilkApp](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/functions/createSilkApp/)
does it for you), or objects draw one call each, as without batching.

### Returns

`void`

### Example

```ts
import { enableSilkBatching, SilkGraphics } from 'pixi-silk';

enableSilkBatching();
const app = new Application();
await app.init();
```

## horizontal (Function, `pixi-silk`)

URL: https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/functions/horizontal/

```ts
import { horizontal } from 'pixi-silk';
```

```ts
function horizontal(stops: StopInput[], options?: Omit<LinearGradientOptions, "stops" | "from" | "to">): LinearGradient;
```

Left-to-right linear gradient across each painted shape's box.

### Parameters

| Parameter | Type |
| ------ | ------ |
| `stops` | [`StopInput`](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/types/StopInput/)[] |

## mesh (Function, `pixi-silk`)

URL: https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/functions/mesh/

```ts
import { mesh } from 'pixi-silk';
```

```ts
function mesh(
   cols: number, 
   rows: number, 
   colors: MeshColorInput[], 
   options?: MeshGradientOptions
): MeshGradient;
```

Gradient mesh: `cols` by `rows` control colours (row by row, top-left first) spread over the
painted shape's box, blended into one smooth surface. `cols` and `rows` are clamped to 1..16.
Missing colours repeat the last one.

### Parameters

| Parameter | Type |
| ------ | ------ |
| `cols` | `number` |
| `rows` | `number` |
| `colors` | [`MeshColorInput`](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/types/MeshColorInput/)[] |
| `options` | [`MeshGradientOptions`](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/interfaces/MeshGradientOptions/) |

### Returns

[`MeshGradient`](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/classes/MeshGradient/)

### Example

```ts
// a light beam that fades at the sides and towards the top
const beam = mesh(3, 3, [
    [0xffd6e8, 0], [0xffd6e8, 0], [0xffd6e8, 0],
    [0xffd6e8, 0.2], [0xffd6e8, 0.5], [0xffd6e8, 0.2],
    [0xffe6f0, 0.6], [0xffffff, 1], [0xffe6f0, 0.6],
]);
g.rect(0, 0, 200, 240).fill(beam);
```

## monotoneX (Function, `pixi-silk`)

URL: https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/functions/monotoneX/

```ts
import { monotoneX } from 'pixi-silk';
```

```ts
function monotoneX(flat: number[], step?: number): number[];
```

Monotone cubic interpolation in x (Steffen's method, same family as d3's monotoneX).
Never overshoots the data: peaks stay at the data points, flat runs stay flat.
`step` is the target spacing of the output samples in local units, at most 64 per segment.
Points must be sorted by x. Fewer than 3 points come back as a copy.

### Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default value |
| ------ | ------ | ------ |
| `flat` | `number`[] | `undefined` |
| `step` | `number` | `2` |

### Returns

`number`[]

## Glass (Class, `pixi-silk/glass`)

URL: https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/glass/classes/Glass/

```ts
import { Glass } from 'pixi-silk/glass';
```

A pane of frosted glass from `pixi-silk/glass`. It blurs and bends whatever is drawn behind it,
splits colours at its curved rim, and catches light on the edge that faces the light.

Put labels and icons in [Glass.content](#content). They sit on top of the glass, unblurred. The pane's
top-left corner is at (0, 0). It only sees what was drawn before it in the same frame, so add it
after its backdrop.

On WebGL the pane reads the canvas through the renderer's back buffer. It sets
`renderer.backBuffer.useBackBuffer = true` the first time it draws and shows no glass on that one
frame. Pass `useBackBuffer: true` to the application to have glass from the first frame. The back
buffer costs a full-screen copy each frame for the whole app. WebGPU reads the backdrop without a
back buffer. Any other renderer gets a plain frosted fill instead.

```ts
const pane = new Glass({ width: 320, height: 200, radius: 32 });
pane.content.addChild(label);
app.stage.addChild(backdrop, pane);
```

### Extends

- `Container`

### Constructors

#### Constructor

```ts
new Glass(options?: GlassOptions): Glass;
```

##### Parameters

| Parameter | Type |
| ------ | ------ |
| `options` | [`GlassOptions`](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/glass/interfaces/GlassOptions/) |

##### Returns

`Glass`

##### Overrides



Resizes the pane, in local units, and redraws its outline and shadow. Returns this.

##### Parameters

| Parameter | Type |
| ------ | ------ |
| `width` | `number` |
| `height` | `number` |

##### Returns

`this`

***

#### set()

```ts
set(style: GlassStyle): this;
```

Merges `style` into the current style. Fields left out keep their value. Only a change of
radius, smoothing, shadow or opacity redraws the outline (frost and tint too in the fallback fill).
The rest goes to the filter on the next frame. Returns this.

##### Parameters

| Parameter | Type |
| ------ | ------ |
| `style` | [`GlassStyle`](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/glass/interfaces/GlassStyle/) |

##### Returns

`this`

## GlassStyle (Interface, `pixi-silk/glass`)

URL: https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/glass/interfaces/GlassStyle/

```ts
import type { GlassStyle } from 'pixi-silk/glass';
```

How a [Glass](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/glass/classes/Glass/) pane looks. Distances are in local units and scale with the pane's transform.
Every field is optional. [resolveGlass](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/glass/functions/resolveGlass/) fills in [GLASS\_DEFAULTS](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/glass/variables/GLASS_DEFAULTS/) and clamps the ranges.

|  `tint?` | `ColorSource` | Tint colour, any Pixi colour source. Default white. | [glass/options.ts:26](https://github.com/schmooky/pixi-silk/blob/main/packages/pixi-silk/src/glass/options.ts#L26) |
|  `tintAmount?` | `number` | How much tint to mix in, 0 to 1. Default 0.04. | [glass/options.ts:28](https://github.com/schmooky/pixi-silk/blob/main/packages/pixi-silk/src/glass/options.ts#L28) |

## GLASS_DEFAULTS (Variable, `pixi-silk/glass`)

```ts
import { GLASS_DEFAULTS } from 'pixi-silk/glass';
```

Default values of [GlassStyle](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/glass/interfaces/GlassStyle/), tuned for a pane over bright, colourful content. The tint default is white.

## Aurora (Class, `pixi-silk/glow`)

URL: https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/glow/classes/Aurora/

```ts
import { Aurora } from 'pixi-silk/glow';
```

Light rising from the bottom of a box in three colours. The blobs blend additively, so the light
burns to white where it is strongest. A mask clips it to the box. It drifts while `speed` is not 0
and redraws every blob each frame.

### Extends

- `Container`

### Constructors

#### Constructor

```ts
new Aurora(options: AuroraOptions): Aurora;
```

##### Parameters

| Parameter | Type |
| ------ | ------ |
| `options` | [`AuroraOptions`](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/glow/interfaces/AuroraOptions/) |

##### Returns

`Aurora`

##### Overrides

```ts
Container.constructor
```

### Methods

#### destroy()

```ts
destroy(options?: DestroyOptions): void;
```

Removes all internal references and listeners as well as removes children from the display list.
Do not use a Container after calling `destroy`.

##### Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| ------ | ------ | ------ |
| `options?` | `DestroyOptions` | Options parameter. A boolean will act as if all options have been set to that value |

##### Returns

`void`

##### Example

```ts
container.destroy();
container.destroy(true);
container.destroy({ children: true });
container.destroy({ children: true, texture: true, textureSource: true });
```

##### Overrides

```ts
Container.destroy
```

***

#### set()

```ts
set(options: Partial<Omit<AuroraOptions, "ticker">>): this;
```

Merges new colours, rise, speed, size or radius and redraws. The ticker cannot change. Returns this.

##### Parameters

| Parameter | Type |
| ------ | ------ |
| `options` | `Partial`\<`Omit`\<[`AuroraOptions`](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/glow/interfaces/AuroraOptions/), `"ticker"`\>\> |

##### Returns

`this`

***

#### tick()

```ts
tick(dt: number): boolean;
```

Advances by `dt` seconds, clamped to 0..0.1, for `ticker: null`. Returns false when `speed` is 0.

##### Parameters

| Parameter | Type |
| ------ | ------ |
| `dt` | `number` |

##### Returns

`boolean`

## Glow (Class, `pixi-silk/glow`)

URL: https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/glow/classes/Glow/

```ts
import { Glow } from 'pixi-silk/glow';
```

A shape drawn as a stack of passes from `pixi-silk/glow`: blurred blooms behind, a solid core,
hot highlights on top. Each pass is one child [SilkGraphics](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/classes/SilkGraphics/), so a glow costs one draw call
per pass unless batching merges them.

```ts
const glow = new Glow({ draw: (g) => g.circle(0, 0, 40), layers: neon(0xff3df5) });
```

### Extends

- `Container`

### Constructors

#### Constructor

```ts
new Glow(options: GlowOptions): Glow;
```

##### Parameters

| Parameter | Type |
| ------ | ------ |
| `options` | [`GlowOptions`](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/glow/interfaces/GlowOptions/) |

##### Returns

`Glow`

##### Overrides

```ts
Container.constructor
```

### Accessors

#### passes

##### Get Signature

```ts
get passes(): readonly SilkGraphics[];
```

One graphics per pass, back to front. Read-only, rebuilt by [Glow.redraw](#redraw).

##### Returns

readonly [`SilkGraphics`](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/classes/SilkGraphics/)[]

### Methods

#### redraw()

```ts
redraw(): this;
```

Clears and draws every pass again. Call it when the shape drawn by `draw` changes. Returns this.

##### Returns

`this`

***

#### setDraw()

```ts
setDraw(draw: (g: SilkGraphics) => void): this;
```

Replaces the draw function and redraws every pass. Returns this.

##### Parameters

| Parameter | Type |
| ------ | ------ |
| `draw` | (`g`: [`SilkGraphics`](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/classes/SilkGraphics/)) => `void` |

##### Returns

`this`

***

#### setLayers()

```ts
setLayers(layers: GlowLayer[]): this;
```

Replaces the passes and redraws. Adds or destroys pass graphics to match the new count. Returns this.

##### Parameters

| Parameter | Type |
| ------ | ------ |
| `layers` | [`GlowLayer`](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/glow/interfaces/GlowLayer/)[] |

##### Returns

`this`

## auroraBlobs (Function, `pixi-silk/glow`)

URL: https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/glow/functions/auroraBlobs/

```ts
import { auroraBlobs } from 'pixi-silk/glow';
```

```ts
function auroraBlobs(
   t: number, 
   width: number, 
   height: number, 
   rise?: number
): AuroraBlob[];
```

Where the nine blobs of an aurora sit at time `t` (seconds) in a `width` by `height` box. Light
rises from the bottom: deep colour high and wide, white low and thin. `rise`, 0 to 1, sets how
high it reaches (default 0.62). Pure function: it allocates a new array and draws nothing.

### Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default value |
| ------ | ------ | ------ |
| `t` | `number` | `undefined` |
| `width` | `number` | `undefined` |
| `height` | `number` | `undefined` |
| `rise` | `number` | `0.62` |

### Returns

[`AuroraBlob`](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/glow/interfaces/AuroraBlob/)[]

```ts
function drop(

   cy: number, 
   r: number, 
   tip?: number
```

Adds a drop with its tip up as one closed path and returns `g`. It is a circle of radius `r` around

## fan (Function, `pixi-silk/glow`)

URL: https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/glow/functions/fan/

```ts
import { fan } from 'pixi-silk/glow';
```

```ts
function fan(
   x: number, 
   y: number, 
   angle: number, 
   spread: number, 
   length: number, 
   count: number, 
   width?: number
): Ray[];
```

`count` rays fanning out from (x, y) around `angle` (radians), `spread` radians wide in all, each
`length` long. Neighbouring rays touch at their ends. `width` is the total width at the start,
shared between the rays (default 0, a point). Pair with [spectrum](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/glow/functions/spectrum/) for the colours.

### Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default value |
| ------ | ------ | ------ |
| `x` | `number` | `undefined` |
| `y` | `number` | `undefined` |
| `angle` | `number` | `undefined` |
| `spread` | `number` | `undefined` |
| `length` | `number` | `undefined` |
| `count` | `number` | `undefined` |
| `width` | `number` | `0` |

### Returns

[`Ray`](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/glow/interfaces/Ray/)[]

## neon (Function, `pixi-silk/glow`)

URL: https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/glow/functions/neon/

```ts
import { neon } from 'pixi-silk/glow';
```

```ts
function neon(color: ColorSource, options?: NeonOptions): GlowLayer[];
```

A neon glow as seven [GlowLayer](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/glow/interfaces/GlowLayer/)s, back to front, for a shape about `size` wide. Two blooms
go behind. Then come two coloured drop glows and the core, a radial gradient with a pale inner
shadow. A 60% white copy on top makes the middle burn towards white. A thin blurred white outline
finishes it. On a `dark` surface the glows blend additively.

### Parameters

| Parameter | Type |
| ------ | ------ |
| `color` | `ColorSource` |
| `options` | [`NeonOptions`](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/glow/interfaces/NeonOptions/) |

### Returns

[`GlowLayer`](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/glow/interfaces/GlowLayer/)[]

## shadowStack (Function, `pixi-silk/glow`)

URL: https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/glow/functions/shadowStack/

```ts
import { shadowStack } from 'pixi-silk/glow';
```

```ts
function shadowStack(
   color?: ColorSource, 
   stack?: [number, number][], 
   alpha?: number
): GlowLayer[];
```

Stacked additive shadows behind a shape, as in CSS. Each `[blur, spread]` pair uses the CSS blur
radius, which is twice the gaussian sigma. The default stack is `[8, 0]`, `[32, 8]` and
`[128, 32]` in white at alpha 0.6.

### Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default value |
| ------ | ------ | ------ |
| `color` | `ColorSource` | `0xffffff` |
| `stack` | \[`number`, `number`\][] | `...` |
| `alpha` | `number` | `0.6` |

### Returns

[`GlowLayer`](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/glow/interfaces/GlowLayer/)[]

## GlowLayer (Interface, `pixi-silk/glow`)

URL: https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/glow/interfaces/GlowLayer/

```ts
import type { GlowLayer } from 'pixi-silk/glow';
```

One pass of a [Glow](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/glow/classes/Glow/): the same shape filled or stroked once more, optionally blurred,
scaled and blended additively. Stack a few and a flat shape starts to emit light.

### Properties

| Property | Type | Description | Defined in |
| ------ | ------ | ------ | ------ |
|  `alpha?` | `number` | Opacity of the whole pass, 0 to 1. Default 1. | [glow/Glow.ts:22](https://github.com/schmooky/pixi-silk/blob/main/packages/pixi-silk/src/glow/Glow.ts#L22) |
|  `blend?` | `BLEND_MODES` | Blend mode of the pass. `add` sums light, so overlaps burn towards white. Default `normal`. | [glow/Glow.ts:14](https://github.com/schmooky/pixi-silk/blob/main/packages/pixi-silk/src/glow/Glow.ts#L14) |
|  `fill?` | [`FillInput`](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/types/FillInput/) | Fill of this pass: colour, gradient, alpha and blur, as in `SilkGraphics.fill`. Left out, the pass is not filled. | [glow/Glow.ts:10](https://github.com/schmooky/pixi-silk/blob/main/packages/pixi-silk/src/glow/Glow.ts#L10) |
|  `scale?` | `number` | Scale of the pass around [GlowOptions.center](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/glow/interfaces/GlowOptions/#center). Default 1. | [glow/Glow.ts:16](https://github.com/schmooky/pixi-silk/blob/main/packages/pixi-silk/src/glow/Glow.ts#L16) |
|  `stroke?` | [`StrokeInput`](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/types/StrokeInput/) | Stroke of this pass, as in `SilkGraphics.stroke`. Left out, the pass is not stroked. | [glow/Glow.ts:12](https://github.com/schmooky/pixi-silk/blob/main/packages/pixi-silk/src/glow/Glow.ts#L12) |
|  `x?` | `number` | Horizontal offset of the pass in local units. Default 0. | [glow/Glow.ts:18](https://github.com/schmooky/pixi-silk/blob/main/packages/pixi-silk/src/glow/Glow.ts#L18) |
|  `y?` | `number` | Vertical offset of the pass in local units. Default 0. | [glow/Glow.ts:20](https://github.com/schmooky/pixi-silk/blob/main/packages/pixi-silk/src/glow/Glow.ts#L20) |
