## InnerShadow (Interface, `pixi-silk`)

URL: https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/interfaces/InnerShadow/

```ts
import type { InnerShadow } from 'pixi-silk';
```

A shadow drawn inside the shape from its own distance field, with Figma's semantics. The shape is
moved by `x` and `y`, shrunk by `spread` and blurred. What it no longer covers is shaded.

### Properties

| Property | Type | Description | Defined in |
| ------ | ------ | ------ | ------ |
|  `alpha?` | `number` | Opacity from 0 to 1. Default 1. | [SilkGraphics.ts:66](https://github.com/schmooky/pixi-silk/blob/main/packages/pixi-silk/src/SilkGraphics.ts#L66) |
|  `blend?` | `"normal"` \| `"add"` | `add` paints it plus-lighter: it brightens what is underneath. Default `normal`. | [SilkGraphics.ts:76](https://github.com/schmooky/pixi-silk/blob/main/packages/pixi-silk/src/SilkGraphics.ts#L76) |
|  `blur?` | `number` | Blur (standard deviation, local units). Default 0. | [SilkGraphics.ts:72](https://github.com/schmooky/pixi-silk/blob/main/packages/pixi-silk/src/SilkGraphics.ts#L72) |
|  `color?` | `ColorSource` | Colour, any Pixi `ColorSource`. Default black. | [SilkGraphics.ts:64](https://github.com/schmooky/pixi-silk/blob/main/packages/pixi-silk/src/SilkGraphics.ts#L64) |
|  `spread?` | `number` | Grows the shadow inwards. Negative values make it thinner. Default 0. | [SilkGraphics.ts:74](https://github.com/schmooky/pixi-silk/blob/main/packages/pixi-silk/src/SilkGraphics.ts#L74) |
|  `x?` | `number` | Horizontal offset, local units. Positive moves the shadow right. Default 0. | [SilkGraphics.ts:68](https://github.com/schmooky/pixi-silk/blob/main/packages/pixi-silk/src/SilkGraphics.ts#L68) |
|  `y?` | `number` | Vertical offset, local units. Positive moves the shadow down. Default 0. | [SilkGraphics.ts:70](https://github.com/schmooky/pixi-silk/blob/main/packages/pixi-silk/src/SilkGraphics.ts#L70) |

## ProgressiveBlur (Interface, `pixi-silk`)

```ts
import type { ProgressiveBlur } from 'pixi-silk';
```

A blur that changes across the shape, like Figma's progressive layer blur. The radius goes from

## ColorSpace (Type, `pixi-silk`)

URL: https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/types/ColorSpace/

```ts
import type { ColorSpace } from 'pixi-silk';
```

```ts
type ColorSpace = "oklab" | "srgb" | "linear";
```

Colour space gradients are interpolated in: perceptual OKLab (default), linear light, or plain sRGB.

## Easing (Type, `pixi-silk`)

URL: https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/types/Easing/

```ts
import type { Easing } from 'pixi-silk';
```

```ts
type Easing = "linear" | "smooth" | ((t: number) => number);
```

How the ramp moves between stops.

- `linear`: piecewise linear between stops (CSS behaviour).
- `smooth`: monotone cubic spline through the stops with eased ends. Removes the
  Mach bands you see at every stop of a linear ramp and never overshoots.
- a function remaps the gradient parameter 0..1 before lookup, for example an easing curve
  for scrims. Reuse one function instance: each new function bakes a new atlas row.

## ExtendMode (Type, `pixi-silk`)

URL: https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/types/ExtendMode/

```ts
import type { ExtendMode } from 'pixi-silk';
```

```ts
type ExtendMode = "pad" | "repeat" | "reflect";
```

What a gradient does outside 0..1: hold the end colours (`pad`), tile (`repeat`) or mirror (`reflect`).

## enableWebGPU (Function, `pixi-silk/webgpu`)

URL: https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/webgpu/functions/enableWebGPU/

```ts
import { enableWebGPU } from 'pixi-silk/webgpu';
```

```ts
function enableWebGPU(): void;
```

Lets SilkGraphics render with Pixi's WebGPU renderer. It installs the WGSL version of the
shader, which lives in this module so that WebGL2 apps never download it.

[createSilkApp](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/functions/createSilkApp/) calls it for you when Pixi picks WebGPU. If you create the Pixi
application yourself, call it once before you create any SilkGraphics. Objects created before
the call have no WebGPU program, and Pixi skips them with a warning.

### Returns

`void`

### Example

```ts
import { Application } from 'pixi.js';
import { SilkGraphics } from 'pixi-silk';
import { enableWebGPU } from 'pixi-silk/webgpu';

const app = new Application();
await app.init({ preference: 'webgpu' });
enableWebGPU();
app.stage.addChild(new SilkGraphics().circle(50, 50, 40).fill(0x30d158));
```

## isWebGPUEnabled (Function, `pixi-silk/webgpu`)

URL: https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/webgpu/functions/isWebGPUEnabled/

```ts
import { isWebGPUEnabled } from 'pixi-silk/webgpu';
```

```ts
function isWebGPUEnabled(): boolean;
```

Whether [enableWebGPU](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/webgpu/functions/enableWebGPU/) has run, so new SilkGraphics carry a WebGPU program.

### Returns

`boolean`

---

# FAQ

## What is pixi-silk?

An MIT-licensed TypeScript library for PixiJS v8. Its `SilkGraphics` display object has a Graphics-like API and draws each shape as a distance field, anti-aliased per pixel in the shader.

## Is pixi-silk a replacement for Graphics?

For UI, chart and icon drawing, yes: `SilkGraphics` keeps the active path, `fill()` and `stroke()`. It has no texture fills and no `svg()` import (`svgPath(d)` reads one path string), and both classes work side by side.

## Which entry point do I import?

The root `pixi-silk` import holds SilkGraphics, gradients, `createSilkApp` and batching. Text, layout, glass, glow, WebGPU and every UI widget are separate entry points, such as `pixi-silk/text` or `pixi-silk/ui/gizmo`, so an app bundles only what it imports.

## Can I use pixi-silk in React, Vue or Svelte?

Yes. Create the app in a mount hook with `createSilkApp({ parent: element })` and call its `destroy()` on unmount.

## What license is pixi-silk under?

MIT, for commercial and open-source use.

## How do I draw a squircle (iOS-style rounded rectangle) in PixiJS?

Call `g.roundRect(x, y, width, height, radius, smoothing)` with smoothing between 0 and 1. iOS uses about 0.6.

## Why do thin lines flicker or disappear in PixiJS?

A line thinner than one device pixel covers only part of each pixel, so sampling hits some pixels and misses others. SilkGraphics keeps such hairlines one pixel wide and lowers their opacity with their width.

## Can SilkGraphics fill a free-form path?

Yes. A path from `moveTo()`, `lineTo()`, the curve calls or `svgPath(d)` fills with the even-odd rule and strokes with miter, bevel or round joins.

## How do I cut one shape out of another?

Use `g.boolean('subtract', a, b)` with two callbacks that draw the shapes, or pass `op` to `fill()`. Union, intersect, subtract and exclude are supported.

## How do I make gradients in PixiJS without banding?

Fill with `linear`, `radial`, `conic` or `along` from pixi-silk. Gradients are baked into a half-float atlas and dithered by half an 8-bit step, which hides the bands in dark, wide ramps.

## How do I add a glow or soft shadow without a filter?

Give the paint a `blur`, for example `g.circle(0, 0, 40).fill({ color: 0xff375f, blur: 12 })`. Add `spread` to grow the shape before the blur.

## Are glass and glow part of the root import?

No. Glass lives in `pixi-silk/glass` and glow in `pixi-silk/glow`. Both are filters, so they cost a render pass where plain blur does not.

## Does pixi-silk work with WebGPU?

Yes. Pass `preference: 'webgpu'` to `createSilkApp`, or call `enableWebGPU()` from `pixi-silk/webgpu` before the first SilkGraphics in your own Pixi app. WebGL2 is the default and the fallback.

## How do I draw many SilkGraphics in one draw call?

Call `enableSilkBatching()` before you create the objects. It is off by default and works on WebGL2 and WebGPU. Without it, each SilkGraphics is one instanced draw call.

## Why is my PixiJS canvas blurry on retina or high-DPI screens?

The canvas backing store does not match the device pixels, or a filter renders at resolution 1. `createSilkApp` sizes the canvas from `devicePixelContentBoxSize` and makes filters inherit the screen resolution.

## Does pixi-silk need antialias: true?

No. Coverage is computed per pixel, so create the app with `antialias: false`, as `createSilkApp` does. MSAA would only cost memory bandwidth.

## How do I enable anti-aliasing in PixiJS v8?

Pass `antialias: true` to `app.init()` for MSAA on the main canvas, with `resolution: window.devicePixelRatio` and `autoDensity: true` for retina screens. MSAA skips filters and render textures unless you opt them in.

## Why do PixiJS v8 Graphics look jagged or blurry?

Graphics are tessellated into triangles, and only MSAA smooths their edges. Scaled curves show facets, thin lines crawl between pixels, and filters render at resolution 1 by default.

## What is analytic anti-aliasing?

Each edge pixel's coverage is computed from the shape's geometry, not from a few samples. pixi-silk divides the signed distance to the shape by the size of one device pixel.

## Is there a PixiJS v8 version of @pixi/graphics-smooth?

`@pixi/graphics-smooth` targets PixiJS v7, and its 1.1 line needs PixiJS 7.2 or a newer v7. SilkGraphics has a v8-style `fill()` and `stroke()` API.
